title: AF-School-final(B243)
description: Airframe comprehensive school-final exam spanning multiple modules: structures and sheet metal repair, composites, hydraulics/pneumatics, landing gear, flight controls, air conditioning/pressurization, fuel systems, fire protection, weight and balance, rigging, and aircraft inspection/documentation, drawn from the AF School-Final (B-243) question/answer bank.

questions.question: When considering weight needed forward and aft of the aircraft for balance purposes, which occupant's position is a key variable load?
questions.explanation: The pilot's weight and seating position is one of the key variable loads considered when computing the aircraft's forward/aft balance.

questions.question: In a mechanical feel system, what counters the upward movement of the servo valve?
questions.explanation: In certain mechanical feel system designs, pitot (airspeed-related) pressure acts against the servo valve's movement, providing speed-appropriate resistance.

questions.question: What shows fuel flow in the fuel system?
options: A. The fuel quantity indicating system
B. The fuel flow indication system
C. The fuel pressure warning light
questions.explanation: A dedicated fuel flow indication system measures and displays the real-time rate of fuel consumption to the crew.

questions.question: Cowl plates/cowl flaps are typically made of what material?
questions.explanation: Engine cowl plates and cowl flaps are commonly constructed of lightweight, heat-tolerant aluminum alloy.

questions.question: Cabin pressure, expressed in terms of altitude, is measured by what instrument?
questions.explanation: Cabin pressure is converted into an equivalent altitude reading and displayed using a cabin altimeter.

questions.question: What is a function of wash primer, and what does it not require?
options: A. It passivates (prepares) the surface and does not require sanding before further coating
B. It provides the final gloss color and must always be sanded
C. It replaces the need for any topcoat
questions.explanation: Wash primer chemically treats (passivates) bare metal to improve corrosion resistance and paint adhesion, and is formulated so it does not need sanding before subsequent coats.

questions.question: Acetone, MEK (methyl ethyl ketone), and similar solvents are characterized by what property?
options: A. High flash point, non-flammable liquids
B. Low flash point (highly flammable) liquids
questions.explanation: These common shop solvents are volatile and highly flammable, meaning they have a low flash point requiring careful handling.

questions.question: In sheet metal repair, which of the following is NOT a preferred practice?
options: A. Matching the original material thickness
C. Making a weld repair too strong (over-strengthened relative to the surrounding structure)
questions.explanation: An overly strong (stiff) weld repair can create a hard spot that concentrates stress in the surrounding, more flexible structure, making it an undesirable repair practice.

questions.question: Aircraft windows and canopies are commonly made from what material?
options: C. Polycarbonate exclusively, with no acrylic use
questions.explanation: Acrylic (often known by trade names like Plexiglass) is the common transparent material used for aircraft windows and canopies.

questions.question: What comes first when installing a landing gear?
options: A. Installing the wheel and tire
questions.explanation: Before installing the landing gear, the mounting structure/area must first be inspected to confirm it is in proper condition to accept the gear.

questions.question: Which document provides the range (limits) of control surface travel?
options: A. The weight and balance report
questions.explanation: The AMM specifies the approved control surface travel ranges and rigging data used during inspection and maintenance.

questions.question: Which valve is used to control the pack (air conditioning) outlet temperature?
questions.explanation: The TBV regulates how much air bypasses the ACM turbine section, directly controlling the pack's final outlet temperature.

questions.question: What happens when the low limit control valve senses a temperature greater than 35°F?
options: A. It does not add heat; the low limit control valve adds heat only when temperature is at or below 35°F to the water separator
B. It always adds heat regardless of temperature
C. It shuts off all bleed air
questions.explanation: The low limit control valve adds heat to protect the water separator from freezing only when sensed temperature drops to or below about 35°F; above that, no extra heat is needed.

questions.question: A fairlead should never deflect a control cable from a straight line by more than what angle?
questions.explanation: Standard practice limits fairlead-induced cable deflection to no more than about 3 degrees from a straight line, minimizing wear and friction.

questions.question: A turnbuckle should never have exposed threads on either side of the barrel exceeding how many threads?
questions.explanation: Standard rigging practice limits visible/exposed turnbuckle threads to no more than 3 on either side of the barrel, ensuring adequate thread engagement.

questions.question: If total moment is 128,000 and weight is 3,200, what is the CG location?
questions.explanation: CG = total moment / total weight = 128,000 / 3,200 = 40, giving the center of gravity location in the units used for the moment/weight calculation.

questions.question: What causes blisters or bubbles in a paint finish?
options: A. Using too thin a paint
B. Oil or water contamination in the spray gun's air line
C. Allowing too long a drying time between coats
questions.explanation: Moisture or oil carried in the compressed air supply to the spray gun can become trapped under the paint film, forming blisters or bubbles as it tries to escape.

questions.question: An airworthiness certificate must conform to what?
options: C. The type of certificate (type certificate) issued for that aircraft
questions.explanation: The airworthiness certificate is tied to and must conform to the aircraft's type certificate and its approved configuration.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly matches an inspection finding with its repair action?
options: A. A leaking packing seal is repaired by repainting the surface
B. A leaking packing seal is repaired by adding more lubricant only
C. A leaking packing seal is repaired by replacing the packing
questions.explanation: A worn or leaking packing (dynamic seal) is properly corrected by replacing the packing itself, not by cosmetic or unrelated fixes.

questions.question: What is a hybrid composite?
options: A. A composite using only one fiber type throughout
B. A composite with no resin matrix at all
C. A combination of two different reinforcement fiber types in the same matrix
questions.explanation: A hybrid composite blends two (or more) distinct reinforcement fiber types (such as carbon and aramid) within a single shared resin matrix.

questions.question: What type of seal is a Chevron seal?
questions.explanation: Chevron (V-ring) seals are designed to seal effectively in one direction, due to their V-shaped lip geometry.

questions.question: What color is an oxygen hose typically coded?
questions.explanation: Oxygen system hoses are conventionally color-coded green, distinguishing them from other system lines such as fuel (red) or hydraulic lines.

questions.question: An oxygen pressure regulator typically has two indicators: one showing cylinder pressure, and what else?
questions.explanation: The second gauge on an oxygen regulator shows the reduced working/delivery pressure supplied downstream, as distinct from the raw cylinder storage pressure.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT true about the receiver drier in a vapor cycle system?
options: A. That it separates the high and low pressure sections of the system (that is the compressor's role, not the receiver drier's)
B. That it stores liquid refrigerant as a reservoir
C. That it contains a desiccant to remove moisture
questions.explanation: The receiver drier stores refrigerant and removes moisture but does not itself act as the boundary between high and low pressure sides; the compressor performs that function.

questions.question: Which component separates the high-pressure and low-pressure sides of a vapor cycle system?
questions.explanation: The compressor marks the transition point between the low-pressure refrigerant entering and the high-pressure refrigerant leaving, forming the system's pressure boundary.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT considered a source of ignition?
options: A. Static discharge (this is actually a recognized ignition source, making it the exception/false choice)
questions.explanation: Static discharge is, in fact, a well-recognized potential ignition source for flammable vapors, so identifying it as "not" a source is the false/exception statement among typical ignition sources.

questions.question: What does CDCCL (Critical Design Configuration Control Limitation) provide?
options: A. A schedule for routine 100-hour inspections
B. A list of approved paint colors
C. Instructions to retain the critical ignition source prevention feature during configuration changes caused by alterations, repairs, or maintenance actions
questions.explanation: CDCCLs identify design features critical to preventing fuel tank ignition sources and specify limitations ensuring those features aren't compromised by maintenance, repairs, or alterations.

questions.question: What does pulling a manual gear extension handle do?
options: A. Releases the gear's mechanical uplock
questions.explanation: The manual extension handle releases the mechanical uplock, allowing the landing gear to free-fall and lock down independent of hydraulic power.

questions.question: When ice is detected by the aircraft's ice detection system, what happens?
options: B. An annunciator light comes on to alert the crew
questions.explanation: Ice detection systems alert the crew through an annunciator light, prompting them to activate the appropriate anti-ice/de-ice systems.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a purpose of the outflow valve?
options: A. Introducing outside air into the cabin
C. Allowing air to exit the cabin at a controlled rate
questions.explanation: The outflow valve controls air leaving the cabin to regulate pressure; it does not introduce outside air into the cabin, which is the function of the bleed air/pack supply system.

questions.question: What is used to reduce the curing time of a bonded honeycomb repair from about 12 hours down to about 1 hour?
questions.explanation: Infrared heat lamps deliver concentrated, controlled heat to the repair area, dramatically shortening the cure time compared with ambient/room-temperature curing.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT drained overboard through drain masts?
options: A. Waste water from the toilet (handled by the dedicated vacuum waste system, not simple drain masts)
questions.explanation: Toilet waste is handled through the separate vacuum waste system, while drain masts handle relatively clean water such as galley sink drainage and condensation.

questions.question: While checking the accumulator, what do you usually check regarding the system?
options: B. The accumulator's serial number only
C. The accumulator's air (gas) precharge pressure
questions.explanation: A key accumulator check is verifying that its air/gas precharge pressure is correctly set to specification.

questions.question: Which type of system commonly uses a vane-type pump?
options: C. A system with no pump at all
questions.explanation: Vane-type pumps are commonly used in relatively low-pressure, higher-volume applications compared with piston-type pumps used for higher pressure needs.

questions.question: In sheet metal repair, why is making a repair "too strong" not desirable?
options: A. Because an overly strong (stiff) repair is undesirable, as it can create a hard spot that concentrates stress in the surrounding structure
B. Because it always costs less to make repairs weaker
C. Because strong repairs always weigh less
questions.explanation: A repair that is excessively stiff/strong compared with the surrounding structure can create a stress concentration point, potentially causing fatigue cracking nearby.

questions.question: How do you confirm the CG is in the correct (safe) position across its expected range of loading?
options: A. By performing an adverse-loaded CG check
B. By performing a simple visual inspection only
C. By checking the tire pressure
questions.explanation: An adverse-loaded CG check loads the aircraft to its extreme forward and aft limits to confirm the CG stays within approved bounds under worst-case loading scenarios.

questions.question: When the airplane's external pressure decreases to within about 0.25 psi of the selected flight altitude's target differential, what flight phase is this generally associated with?
questions.explanation: As the aircraft approaches its target cruise differential pressure during climb, this condition is associated with reaching and settling into the cruise flight phase.

questions.question: Which type of stall warning system is commonly used on light aircraft?
options: A. A pneumatic stall warning system
B. A full digital fly-by-wire stall protection computer
C. A radar-based stall detection system
questions.explanation: Many light aircraft use a simple pneumatic (reed horn) stall warning device triggered by airflow changes as the stall angle of attack is approached.

questions.question: Leading edge (LE) device surfaces are fully retracted during which phase, and extended during which phase to increase lift?
options: A. Retracted during takeoff, extended during cruise
B. Retracted during cruise, extended during takeoff (and landing)
C. Retracted during landing, extended during cruise
questions.explanation: Leading edge devices (slats) stay retracted for low-drag cruise flight and are extended during takeoff and landing to increase lift at lower airspeeds.

questions.question: What is the width of material measured around all the bends, from edge to edge, called?
questions.explanation: Total developed width is the overall flat-pattern width required to form a part, accounting for all bends along its cross-section.

questions.question: What type of de-icing system do GA (general aviation) and turboprop commuter-type aircraft often use?
options: A. A full thermal pneumatic bleed air system
B. A pneumatic de-icing system (inflatable boots)
C. An electromagnetic impulse system exclusively
questions.explanation: GA and smaller turboprop commuter aircraft commonly use pneumatic de-ice boots, which are simpler and require less bleed air than large thermal anti-ice systems.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a purpose of cabin pressurization?
options: A. Maintaining a comfortable, physiologically safe cabin altitude
B. Equalizing cabin pressure exactly with ambient (outside) pressure
C. Allowing occupants to function normally at high cruise altitude
questions.explanation: Pressurization exists specifically to maintain a cabin pressure higher than (not equal to) the thin ambient air at altitude; equalizing with ambient pressure is the opposite of pressurization's purpose.

questions.question: Which document helps determine and verify control surface travel limits?
options: A. The weight and balance report
questions.explanation: The AMM specifies the approved control surface travel limits and provides the rigging procedures used to verify and adjust them.

questions.question: A tire chine, mounted on the wheel, is used for what purpose?
options: A. To increase tire traction on dry pavement
B. To deflect runway water sideways, away from the aircraft/engines
questions.explanation: Chine tires have a molded deflector rib that throws water sideways during takeoff/landing roll, helping protect aft-mounted engines from water spray ingestion.

questions.question: Which brake system typically requires a large volume of hydraulic fluid?
options: A. The power brake actuating system
B. A simple master-cylinder-only brake system
C. A mechanical cable brake system
questions.explanation: Power brake systems, which handle larger aircraft and higher brake forces, require a greater volume of hydraulic fluid delivery compared with simple master cylinder systems.

questions.question: In a mechanical Q-feel (artificial feel) system, what determines the amount of force the pilot feels?
options: A. The relative position of a fulcrum (lever ratio)
B. The color of the control cables
questions.explanation: Mechanical feel systems often use a movable fulcrum or linkage ratio, adjusted according to flight conditions (such as airspeed), to vary the force transmitted to the pilot.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT considered a source of ignition?
options: A. Static discharge (actually a recognized ignition source, making it the false/exception choice)
B. A spark from damaged wiring
C. A hot surface from an overheated component
questions.explanation: Static discharge is indeed a recognized potential ignition source for flammable vapors, so a statement excluding it as a source would be the false one among the choices.

questions.question: What is a thin layer of fiberglass cured with a composite repair part to create a clean surface for bonding purposes called?
questions.explanation: Peel ply is bonded onto the laminate and peeled away just before final bonding, leaving behind a clean, properly textured surface ready for adhesion.

questions.question: What describes the construction of a duplex seal?
options: A. A single O-ring with no backup
C. A T-seal with a backup of two Teflon rings
questions.explanation: A duplex seal combines a T-shaped seal element with two supporting Teflon backup rings, providing a robust, durable sealing arrangement for demanding applications.

questions.question: At what pressure does a typical high-pressure hydraulic system normally operate?
questions.explanation: Many aircraft high-pressure hydraulic systems are designed to operate at approximately 3,000 psi, a common standard for transport category aircraft.

questions.question: For a constant-delivery hydraulic pump, what components manage system pressure without continuous full-flow output?
options: A. A cut-out valve and an accumulator
B. A standpipe and a baffle
C. A thermal relief valve alone
questions.explanation: With a constant delivery pump, a cut-out (unloading) valve combined with an accumulator allows the pump to unload once system pressure is reached, avoiding wasted continuous full-flow pumping.

questions.question: What are the components of a simple hydraulic power pack?
options: A. Only a pump and an actuator
B. Only a reservoir and accumulator
C. A pump, reservoir, selector valve, and filter
questions.explanation: A self-contained power pack bundles a pump, reservoir, selector/control valve, and filter together into one compact unit.

questions.question: When does the Turbine Bypass Valve (TBV) operate?
options: A. Only when the aircraft is on the ground
B. When the air conditioning pack is ON
questions.explanation: The TBV is active whenever its associated air conditioning pack is operating, modulating bypass air to control pack outlet temperature.

questions.question: Who is ultimately responsible for setting and enforcing airworthiness regulations?
options: A. A single global authority with no national variation
B. All aviation authorities around the world (each country's regulatory body)
questions.explanation: Each country's aviation authority (such as the FAA, EASA, etc.) is responsible for establishing and enforcing airworthiness regulations within its jurisdiction.

questions.question: What is the difference between a power-assisted brake system and a full power brake system?
options: A. In a power brake system, the pilot feels the full braking load directly
B. In a power-assisted system, the pilot still feels some of the actual braking load/force
C. There is no difference between the two systems
questions.explanation: Power-assisted brakes blend hydraulic boost with some direct pilot-felt force, whereas a full power brake system isolates the pilot from direct brake force feedback entirely.

questions.question: Which component attaches the landing gear to the airframe and allows it to pivot for retraction/extension?
questions.explanation: The trunnion is the structural pivot attachment point on the airframe around which the landing gear leg rotates during retraction and extension.

questions.question: Inspection of wood structure to recognize defects cannot be adequately learned by what means alone?
options: A. Hands-on training combined with reference material
questions.explanation: Reliably recognizing wood defects requires hands-on experience and training, not simply reading about defects in a textbook.

questions.question: What does the "Look" phase of inspection involve?
options: A. Completing paperwork and work orders only
B. Running a full functional test of all systems
C. Visual inspection and touching (tactile) examination of the aircraft/components
questions.explanation: The Look phase is the hands-on, sensory examination stage of inspection, where the technician visually and physically (by touch) assesses the condition of the aircraft.

questions.question: What inspection program divides the full inspection into smaller parts to reduce aircraft ground time?
options: B. A continuous inspection program check
questions.explanation: Progressive inspection breaks the comprehensive annual-equivalent inspection scope into smaller segments performed over time, minimizing how long the aircraft is out of service at any one point.

questions.question: A defect such as insertion of backing paper and separation of films within a laminate is classified as what type of defect?
questions.explanation: Defects traced to problems during original fabrication (such as improperly inserted backing material or film separation) are classified as manufacturing defects.

questions.question: What does envelope bagging refer to in composite repair?
options: A. Bagging only the local repair patch area
B. No vacuum bag is used at all
C. Complete enclosure of the workpiece within the vacuum bag
questions.explanation: Envelope bagging fully encloses the entire part (not just the repair patch) inside the vacuum bag assembly for curing.

questions.question: Which toilet system type is removed from the aircraft and emptied/dumped at an approved disposal area?
options: A. The vacuum toilet type (serviced in place)
questions.explanation: A removable toilet assembly can be taken off the aircraft entirely and emptied/serviced at an approved disposal facility, unlike systems serviced in place.

questions.question: What is the dangerous possibility of exposure associated with radiographic (X-ray) inspection?
questions.explanation: Radiographic inspection uses ionizing radiation, making radiation exposure to personnel the primary safety hazard requiring shielding and controlled access.

questions.question: For how long should the fuel tank be able to provide fuel at maximum continuous power, per certain certification reference standards?
questions.explanation: Certain fuel system adequacy standards reference a minimum endurance margin, such as 30 minutes at maximum continuous power, as part of required fuel system capability.

questions.question: What speeds up the preflight weight and balance computation?
options: C. Re-weighing the aircraft before every flight
questions.explanation: The loading graph method lets pilots quickly read weight and moment/CG values from a chart, speeding up preflight calculations compared with manual computation.

questions.question: In an aircraft, which unit works as a small turbine that provides electrical power and pneumatic power, especially on the ground?
questions.explanation: The APU is a small turbine engine, typically in the tail, supplying electrical and pneumatic power without needing the main engines running, especially useful on the ground.

questions.question: In an aircraft's zonal numbering system, what does Zone 400 typically represent?
questions.explanation: In the standard ATA/manufacturer zonal numbering convention, the 400-series zone numbers are commonly assigned to the power plant/engine area.

questions.question: What is the last part of rigging the elevator?
options: A. The trim tab is removed
B. The cable tension is disconnected
C. The travel is measured (as a final confirming check)
questions.explanation: Elevator rigging concludes with measuring the control surface travel to confirm it falls within the specified limits after adjustments are made.

questions.question: What type of medium-flexible cable is used for engine, trim tab, and indicator controls?
questions.explanation: 7x7 cable's medium flexibility makes it well suited to lighter-duty applications such as engine controls, trim tabs, and indicator systems.

questions.question: What is used when alterations and repairs have moved the Empty Weight CG (EWCG) out of its limits, typically made of lead and painted red?
questions.explanation: Permanent ballast (lead blocks painted red for identification) is installed to bring the empty weight CG back within its approved limits after an alteration shifts it out of range.

questions.question: Which of the following is a requirement for aviation fuel regarding sulfur content?
options: A. High sulfur content for better lubrication
C. Sulfur content is irrelevant to fuel quality
questions.explanation: Aviation fuel specifications call for low sulfur content to minimize corrosive combustion byproducts and reduce engine/component damage.

questions.question: Which type of landing gear arrangement is best suited for applying hard braking without the aircraft nosing over?
questions.explanation: With tricycle gear, the center of gravity sits forward of the main wheels, allowing heavy braking without the risk of the aircraft tipping forward onto its nose.
